?Court No. - 27
Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 485 of 2023
Applicant :- Ashish Kumar And Others
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru.Prin.Secy. Deptt. Of Home And Others Counsel for Applicant :- Lokendra Kumar Gupta,Mirza Humayun Qadar

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Shree Prakash Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

Instant application has been filed with prayer for quashing of the order dated 22.12.2022 passed by Chief Judicial Magistrate, Lucknow as well as chargesheet dated 17.02.2022 submitted under Sections 269, 420 and 34 IPC and 3/4 Epidemic Act in Crime No.48 of 2022, Case No.124629 of 2022, Police Station Hazratganj, District - Lucknow .

sentences.text: Learned counsel appearing for the applicants submits that the applicants are innocent and have falsely been implicated in the instant matter.

He further added that ingredients of Sections 269, 420 and 34 IPC and 3/4 Epidemic Act do not attract in the instant matter and there is no cogent piece of evidence against the applicants but Investigating Officer, without any of the evidence, has filed charge sheet under Sections 269, 420 and 34 IPC and 3/4 Epidemic Act.
He submits that the whole proceedings including filing of the charge sheet as well as summoning order vitiates in the eyes of law and is liable to be quashed.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the State has opposed the contentions aforesaid and submits that there is no abuse of process of law as summoning order as well as charge sheet has rightly been filed and the summoning order has rightly been issued and at this stage, the factual dispute cannot be raised by invoking the jurisdiction under Section 482 Cr.P.C. and thus the application is liable to be dismissed.

After the argument at length, learned counsel for the applicants submits that interest of justice would be sub-served, if the trial court is directed to consider and decide the application of discharge within stipulated period of time, as may be fixed by this Court.
Learned AGA for the State has no objection to the contention aforesaid.

In view of aforesaid submissions, the applicants are permitted to file an application for discharge before the court below within a period of seven days from today, if not already filed, and if such an application is filed, the same shall be decided within a further period of 30 days, strictly in accordance with law.
With the aforesaid observation, the application is disposed off.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
Learned counsel appearing for the applicants submits that the applicants are innocent and have falsely been implicated in the instant matter.
He further added that ingredients of Sections 269, 420 and 34 IPC and 3/4 Epidemic Act do not attract in the instant matter and there is no cogent piece of evidence against the applicants but Investigating Officer, without any of the evidence, has filed charge sheet under Sections 269, 420 and 34 IPC and 3/4 Epidemic Act.
He submits that the whole proceedings including filing of the charge sheet as well as summoning order vitiates in the eyes of law and is liable to be quashed.
On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the State has opposed the contentions aforesaid and submits that there is no abuse of process of law as summoning order as well as charge sheet has rightly been filed and the summoning order has rightly been issued and at this stage, the factual dispute cannot be raised by invoking the jurisdiction under Section 482 Cr.P.C. and thus the application is liable to be dismissed.
After the argument at length, learned counsel for the applicants submits that interest of justice would be sub-served, if the trial court is directed to consider and decide the application of discharge within stipulated period of time, as may be fixed by this Court.

With the aforesaid observation, the application is disposed off.
